title: How to set up goal-based investing for multiple financial targets
description: Aligning your asset allocation with your time horizon using the 'Bucket Strategy'.
content:
Money is fungible—a dollar is a dollar. But in your mind, money is distinct. The dollar for your daughter's wedding feels different than the dollar for your retirement. **Goal-Based Investing** honors this psychology by creating separate 'buckets' for each goal, each with its own investment strategy. Instead of one big messy portfolio, you have a 'House Portfolio' (Conservative), a 'Retirement Portfolio' (Aggressive), and a 'Travel Portfolio' (Cash). This clarity prevents you from taking too much risk with near-term money.

Key Takeaways

  • Horizon dictates Risk: The single most important factor is 'When do I need the money?'. 2 years = Cash. 20 years = Stocks.
  • Mental Accounting is Good: While economists hate it, separating money into named accounts helps regular people stick to the plan and avoid raiding the wrong pot.
  • The 'Glide Path': As you get closer to the goal date (e.g., the wedding), you must shift that specific bucket from stocks to bonds/cash to lock in the win.
  • Automation: You can set up automatic splits. $500 to Retirement, $200 to House, $100 to Car. The robots handle the allocation.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Modern US brokerages (Betterment, Wealthfront, Fidelity) allow you to create multiple 'sub-accounts' or 'goals' under one login. You can name them, set different allocations for each, and track progress bars. This feature is a game changer for goal-based planning.

The 3-Bucket Framework

Stop investing everything in the S&P 500. Match the asset to the timeline.

Bucket 1: Short Term (0-3 Years)

  • Goals: Emergency Fund, Wedding, House Down Payment.
  • Allocation: 100% Cash / Money Market / T-Bills.
  • Why: Return of capital matters more than return on capital. You cannot risk a 20% drop.

Bucket 2: Medium Term (3-10 Years)

  • Goals: Dream Vacation, New Car, Sabbatical.
  • Allocation: 40% Stocks / 60% Bonds (Conservative Mix).
  • Why: You need to beat inflation, but you want to dampen volatility. If the market crashes, you can delay the goal by a year.

Bucket 3: Long Term (10+ Years)

  • Goals: Retirement, Generational Wealth.
  • Allocation: 90-100% Stocks.
  • Why: You have time to recover from crashes. Volatility is the price you pay for maximum growth.

Setup Guide

  1. Audit Your Goals: Write down every major expense >$5,000 you expect in the next 10 years. Put a year next to it.
  2. Open Sub-Accounts: At Fidelity, you can open multiple brokerage accounts. Name them '2030 House', '2040 College'.
  3. Assign Tickers: - 2030 House: Buy AOK (Conservative ETF). - 2040 College: Buy VTI (Total Stock Market).
  4. The Annual Review: Once a year, check the timeline. If the House goal is now only 2 years away, sell the AOK ETF and move to Cash. You are 'landing the plane'.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I just have one big pot?

You can, but it's risky. If the market drops 30%, you might panic and sell everything, ruining your retirement to save your house fund. Separation creates emotional firewalls.

Is this tax efficient?

It can be messy. Multiple accounts mean multiple 1099-DIV forms. Using a Robo-Advisor (Betterment) is often easier because they handle the sub-accounts and tax harvesting automatically in one interface.

What if priorities change?

Just rename the account. 'New Car' becomes 'Baby Fund'. The money is fungible; the label is just for your motivation.
